For lambda>=lambda_a>a, the axial bound makes z1-lambda a negative; this forces lambda²-a lambda<=(1-a)/2. The positive quadratic root is exactly lambda_a=(a+sqrt((1-a)²+1))/2. At that root z=(a-lambda)e1 satisfies the truncation and Euclidean-ball bound for ALL t∈[-1,a] because the squared norm is affine increasing in t when constrained by t²+||y||²<=1; this gives feasibility. Equality in both necessary orbit constraints forces z1=a-lambda and z_perp=0, proving unique center. Monotonicity follows by derivative; the a↓-1 affine blowup tends to paraboloid P_d={0<=s<=1,||y||²<=s}. The direct rim/apex constraints give gamma²+gamma<=1 and a constructive gamma=(sqrt5-1)/2 center, independently of continuity. Independently evaluated the rim equality and maximum-ball inequality for seven truncations, including near-endpoints, with floating error <1e-12. Finite samples only corroborate the analytic universal proof. Dimension one is excluded, and the degenerate endpoint a=-1 is a limit.
